title: AI data readiness checklist
subtitle: Sixteen checks to run before an AI agent touches your data. Tick only what you can show evidence for, not what you believe to be true.
howTo: Pick one AI use case and the data it needs. Answer each check for that data only. A tick needs evidence: a test result, a document, a log.

sections.question: Is the data complete, fresh and consistent enough to answer from?
checks: The tables this use case needs are identified, and each one has a named owner.
Required fields are populated, and you know the null and default rate of each.
Every table has a freshness rule (for example, loaded by 06:00 UTC) and someone is alerted when it is missed.
Figures agree across systems: the same order or invoice totals match in the ERP, the warehouse and the reports.

sections.question: Does the data mean the same thing to every system and every agent?
checks: Each metric the use case needs (margin, revenue, active customer) has one written definition, agreed with finance and the business.
Those definitions are implemented once, in a semantic layer that BI tools and agents both read.
Customers, products and suppliers held in several systems resolve to one record, with the matching rules written down.
Rules an analyst “just knows” are written down: who counts as a customer, intercompany exclusions, the fiscal calendar.

sections.question: Can an agent reach the right data, and only the right data?
checks: Agents run under their own identities, not a shared service account or a person’s credentials.
Row- and column-level permissions are enforced in the data platform, not in the prompt.
Sensitive fields (personal data, pricing, salaries) are classified, and masked where the use case doesn’t need them.
Every agent query is logged: who asked, what data was read and what came back.

sections.question: Can you show where an answer came from, and who owns it?
checks: Lineage runs from every report and agent answer back to the source fields.
Changes to schemas and definitions go through an agreed change process, such as data contracts.
An evaluation set of real questions with known-correct answers runs before go-live and after every change.
A named person monitors answers after go-live and has a route to get problems fixed.

scoring.meaning: Ready to pilot an agent on this data.
Close the unticked checks before go-live, starting with Access.
Start with the data foundation before the agent.

cta.title: Want a second opinion?
cta.body: In a free 45-minute AI Data Readiness Assessment, a senior engineer runs these checks against your own data and shows you what to fix first.
